title: A sparse lane sharing a timeline with dense rows draws every mark as a hairline
foundBy: repository owner, looking at a consuming page's protocol row with traces shown: "they are too squished"

evidence.verified: The browser test that sizes a lane's marks by its own gaps fails on the parent commit and passes here. A protocol lane with `widthBy: "lane"` whose next mark in the timeline is a fifth of a unit away, a sliver at the fit, draws its first mark at the mark size, and the span on the timeline still names it. `npm run ci` passes on cc02010 with every gate run, and the visual gate passes 116 of 116 captures with no differing pixel.

resolution: `widthBy: "lane"` on a lane measures its marks against the next mark in that lane alone, for widths only. The timeline still boxes and walks it.
details:
In the positioned layout a mark is as wide as the gap to the next mark anywhere in its timeline. A consuming page keeps each member as one timeline of a protocol row and several step rows, so a box can frame them all. Every open and reply mark on the protocol row then drew one pixel wide, measured in headless Chromium, because a step follows each within seconds. With the step rows off the same marks drew nine pixels wide.

A lane should be able to measure its marks against the next mark in that lane alone, while staying in its timeline for the box and the arrow keys.
